themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 4 reports THIS WEEK compared to a 0.6-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 540% increase (z-score: 6.97)—signaling a potential pest outbreak emerging in the district.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% spike, z-score 6.97)
Spike is most recent and sharpest in current data cycle
Rodent complaints are reportable, verifiable via 311 records
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected neighborhoods and local exterminators about causes and scope
Investigate whether nearby construction (185% spike in General Construction complaints 2 weeks ago) is displacing rodents into residential areas

themes_detail.label: Mold outbreak across district
themes_detail.summary: Mold complaints exploded to 6 reports last week compared to a 0.1-per-week baseline—a 4,700% increase (z-score: 17.76)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, suggesting widespread moisture/water damage or humidity issues.
evidence: 6 mold complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (4,700% spike, highest z-score at 17.76)
Coincides with elevated Water System complaints (593 total in 90 days) and Sewer issues (165 total)
Heat/Hot Water complaints also elevated (322 in 90 days), suggesting building system failures driving moisture
reporting_angles: Contact affected residents about health impacts and request photo documentation; file FOIL for DOH mold complaints
Investigate whether infrastructure failures (water mains, sewers, heating) are causing water intrusion in buildings; connect to Community Board's repeated DEP budget requests

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 12 reports last week from a 1.1-per-week baseline over 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 8.57)—indicating either vandalism, development activity, or uncontrolled trimming in the district's tree canopy.
evidence: 12 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 8.57)
Bayside/Douglaston/Little Neck are heavily residential with mature tree canopy; organized damage suggests systemic cause
5 active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (189-10 Northern Boulevard, 217-14 24th Avenue, 175-05 Horace Harding, etc.) could indicate development-related tree removal
reporting_angles: Map 311 tree damage complaints to active development sites and rezoning areas; interview Parks Dept about enforcement actions
Interview residents and community gardeners about whether contractors or property owners are illegally trimming trees; investigate permitting gaps

themes_detail.label: Dumpster and sanitation crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints surged to 3 reports THIS WEEK from a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—while Illegal Parking (1,844 total) and Street Condition (1,359) complaints dominate, indicating a breakdown in waste management and street maintenance.
evidence: 3 dumpster complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Illegal Parking (1,844 in 90 days) and Street Condition (1,359 in 90 days) remain top chronic complaints, suggesting systemic neglect
Community Board has repeated budget requests for sanitation infrastructure upgrades, indicating long-standing unmet need
reporting_angles: File FOIL for sanitation truck schedules and missed collections in the district; interview DSNY about staffing and route coverage
Canvass neighborhoods to identify where dumpster overflow is occurring and connect to parking displacement issues

themes_detail.label: Homeless assistance requests accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 5 reports last week from a 0.6-per-week baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.11)—coinciding with a 471% spike in general Safety complaints 3 weeks ago, suggesting an emerging encampment or vulnerable population crisis.
evidence: 5 homeless assistance complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 5.11)
Safety complaints spiked to 5 reports 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (471% spike, z-score 4.45)
Door/Window complaints also elevated 3 weeks ago (9 vs. 2.0 avg), suggesting potential encampment-related break-ins
reporting_angles: Identify where homeless encampments are forming (parks, transit hubs, commercial areas) and interview advocates about causes and services needed
Interview residents about safety concerns and coordinate with NYPD and DHS on outreach and shelter capacity in Queens
